label: New York cheesecake
note: Made with cream cheese; of Ashkenazi Jewish origin in the 1930s

about.text: A baked cheesecake on a cream cheese base, rich and dense, often on a graham-cracker or biscuit crust. Gil Marks traces it to Ashkenazi Jewish cooking of the 1930s, made famous by New York places such as Reuben's and Lindy's.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Cream cheese, sugar and eggs are mixed, poured on a crumb base and baked until the eggs set it; the cream cheese is what gives it the dense, creamy body. Cream cheese itself was only invented in the 1870s, so earlier cheese pies used cottage cheese.
